why:
★ THE SPAN IS PROVENANCE — and TASK 066 changed HOW it is protected: from CHECKING to DERIVING. `L9999-L9999` on a 3-line body used to be accepted at exit 0 and written into `page_entity_refs` AS IF IT WERE PROVENANCE; TASK 064 refused it; TASK 066 DERIVES the span from the (already-verbatim) quote, so a fabricated span is now CORRECTED and the attack is UNREACHABLE rather than merely caught. That is also the kinder outcome: the old refusal cost the operator the WHOLE BATCH for a mechanical mistake the model cannot avoid — it was miscounting lines 29% of the time (33 fresh Haiku contexts, 56 candidates; see evals/baseline.json).

★ SO THIS COUNTEREXAMPLE MOVED. A FABRICATED span is no longer refusable, so grading one would be decorative — and the eval runner caught exactly that, refusing to let an accepted counterexample sit ungraded. What is STILL reachable, and must stay refused, is a MALFORMED span (`"line 8"`): a supplied span is now only a disambiguation HINT, and silently ignoring a malformed hint would be precisely the fail-open this repo keeps having to close.

The property that used to be this fixture's alone is now UNIVERSAL: `test_the_DERIVED_span_ALWAYS_contains_its_own_quote` asserts it for EVERY candidate in EVERY fixture — strictly more coverage than one counterexample ever gave.
